definition: Generative Pre-trained Transformer 1 (GPT-1) is OpenAI's first large language model (LLM) in its GPT series of models, developed following Google's invention of the transformer architecture in 2017.
details: In June 2018, OpenAI released a paper titled "Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training", in which they introduced that initial model along with the term generative pre-trained transformer (GPT). Up to that point, the best-performing neural NLP models primarily employed supervised learning from large amounts of manually labeled data. This reliance on supervised learning limited their use of datasets that were not well-annotated, in addition to making it prohibitively expensive and time-consuming to train extremely large models; many languages (such as Swahili or Haitian Creole) are difficult to translate and interpret using such models due to a lack of available text for corpus-building. In contrast, a GPT's "semi-supervised" approach involved two stages: an unsupervised generative "pre-training" stage in which a language modeling objective was used to set initial parameters, and a supervised discriminative "fine-tuning" stage in which these parameters were adapted to a target task. explainer.lead: GPT-1 was OpenAI's first Generative Pre-trained Transformer and the starting point of its GPT series. Its importance lies in a two-stage recipe: learn language patterns from unlabeled text first, then adapt the resulting model to a specific task with supervised examples.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning a language by reading lots of writing before practicing a particular school exercise. GPT-1 worked similarly: it first learned from text without people labeling every answer, then practiced a chosen task using labeled examples. This made it possible to use text collections that had not been carefully annotated.
tiers.practitioner: The practical recipe is unsupervised language-model pre-training followed by supervised, discriminative fine-tuning for the target task. Pre-training supplies the initial parameters, while fine-tuning adapts them using labeled task data. Do not treat pre-training as eliminating supervision altogether, and do not assume the approach automatically resolves the corpus shortages affecting languages such as Swahili or Haitian Creole.
tiers.paperLevel: GPT-1 uses a transformer architecture and a semi-supervised two-stage objective: maximize a language-modeling objective on unlabeled text to initialize parameters theta, then optimize a supervised discriminative objective to adapt theta to a target task. OpenAI introduced the model and the term generative pre-trained transformer in the June 2018 paper "Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training". Fine-tuning still requires supervision for the target task.

explainer.example: To prepare GPT-1 for a chosen language-understanding task, first train it on unlabeled text so that language modeling sets its initial parameters. Then use labeled examples from that task for supervised fine-tuning, producing parameters adapted to the task rather than training the entire model only from its labeled dataset.

flow: Begin with text that does not require manual task labels.
Pre-train with a language-modeling objective to set initial parameters.
Supply supervised examples for the chosen target task.
Fine-tune the parameters with a discriminative objective.
Use the adapted model for that target task.
explainer.origin: OpenAI introduced GPT-1 in June 2018 in the paper "Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training". The paper also introduced the term generative pre-trained transformer.
explainer.lineage: GPT-1 was the first model in OpenAI's GPT series and followed Google's invention of the transformer architecture in 2017. Its transformer-based approach contrasted with earlier techniques using attention-augmented RNNs.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPT-1 established a way to make broad use of unlabeled text before adapting a model to supervised tasks. This addressed the expense, time, and dataset restrictions created when neural NLP systems depended primarily on large amounts of manually labeled data.
